$comment: Machine-matched term contract between the skills layer (data/skills/**, which EMITS videoDesc) and the prompt layer (data/modelPrompt/video/** + src/lib/prompts/**, which PARSES it). Narrower and stricter than docs/i18n/glossary.json: entries here are tokens code or a model matches on, not prose vocabulary. Verified by `yarn i18n:check-terms`.

countFields.counts: Per-layer raw substring counts of the `zh` form. Recorded as evidence for why the term is here; the checker asserts only the presence rule for the entry's `boundary`, not the exact number.
countFields.literalCounts: Occurrences of the `zh` form in the prompt layer in each of the three locales (the four data/modelPrompt/video files plus the matching locale string of videoPromptGeneration.ts). ASSERTED: en and vi may never fall below the recorded value, because that would mean a matched token was translated away.
countFields.labelCounts: Occurrences of the `en` / `vi` form itself in the corresponding translated prompt files, case-insensitive. Present for translate-label entries only. ASSERTED as a floor, so switching to a second rendering of the same term is caught.
countFields.refresh: After an intentional change run `tsx scripts/i18n-check-terms.ts --update` to rewrite all three count blocks.

srcPrompt.files: the zh locale string of src/lib/prompts/videoPromptGeneration.ts

srcCode.files: src/**/*.ts excluding src/i18n/locales/, promptSeedSync.ts and videoPromptGeneration.ts

policies.keep-zh-literal: The token is matched or emitted verbatim: a value one layer writes into videoDesc and the other matches, or a key the video model must receive character-for-character. It MUST survive translation unchanged — the shipped *.en.md and *.vi.md files carry it in Chinese, at the same count as the zh original. The `en` / `vi` fields are a gloss for talking about the term, NOT a form to write into a file.
policies.translate-label: The token names a position, not a value: the videoDesc fields are delimiter-separated and the field name never appears in the data, so the label is free to be translated. The `en` / `vi` fields ARE the forms the shipped translations use, and the checker asserts they still appear in the translated prompt files. Where the Chinese also survives in a format spec, `literalCounts` pins that minimum too.
policies.translate-in-lockstep: The token IS translated per locale, because its emitter is the i18n catalog rather than a Chinese source file. The `en` / `vi` fields are the runtime forms (see `catalogKey` for the exact catalog entry); the prompt spec that matches them must carry the same locale form. Changing one side without the other breaks matching.
policies.never-translate: The token stays as written in every locale and has no translated form anywhere. `en` and `vi` repeat `zh` deliberately. Reasons: persisted database enum, schema enum, tool name, model identifier, reference syntax or field key.

boundaries.skills-internal: Lives in the skills layer only, but is a near-miss of a boundary token: normalising or translating it would forge (or destroy) a real marker. Listed so a translator leaves it alone.
boundaries.skills->prompts: Emitted by data/skills/**, matched by the prompt layer. Counts must be non-zero in both `skills` and at least one of `modelPrompt` / `srcPrompt`.
boundaries.prompts->model: Emitted by the prompt layer for the downstream video model to consume. Lives in one layer only; included because it is still a literal a translator must preserve.
boundaries.catalog->prompts: Emitted at runtime from src/i18n/locales/*.json, matched by the prompt-layer input-format spec.
boundaries.persisted-enum: Compared against in src/**/*.ts (`.where()`, `===`). Not a pipeline boundary term; listed so no locale ever translates it.
boundaries.schema-enum: Validated by a Zod tool schema and matched by the prompts.
boundaries.model-identifier: Matched against the configured model name by the mode-routing table.
boundaries.reference-syntax: Reference token the model must emit verbatim.

homonymRisk.what: Per-entry field on tokens whose `zh` form is ALSO an ordinary word (or a substring of one) in the source prose. The literal checker counts raw substrings, so those entries generate false positives that a translator must resolve by reading the sentence, not the count.

fields.signals: Concrete surface patterns that mark a hit as prose (or as an unrelated term), each with the reading that applies.
fields.note: How to decide, and what a wrong decision costs.

homonymRisk.rule: When a hit is prose, translate it as prose and record a `literalAllowance` with a written reason in docs/i18n/sidecar-budget.json. NEVER inject the Chinese token into a sentence that is not about the value just to satisfy the count — that teaches the model to bind the token to the wrong concept.

glossary.rule: Where a term exists in both, en/vi must agree. Divergences are recorded per-entry in `glossaryDivergence`.

conflicts.what: The videoDesc field list is written twice — once as the prompt-layer spec tables, once as the Zod describe() text in src/agents/productionAgent/tools.ts via catalog key `agent.production.tools.storyboardPanel.videoDesc`. The two renderings disagree.

conflicts.registryChoice: The registry records the prompt-layer form, because that is the text the parsing model reads. The catalog value should be brought into line; the checker does not yet compare it (see LIMITS).

conflicts.what: Every 景别 mapping table maps BOTH 近景 and 特写 onto the same English tag `close-up`, so two distinct matched values become indistinguishable downstream.
conflicts.registryChoice: The registry keeps them as separate entries with distinct en/vi glosses (Medium close-up / Cận cảnh vs Close-up / Đặc tả) and records the colliding tags under `modelTag`. This is a pre-existing defect in the Chinese originals, not a translation error.

conflicts.what: 全景 maps to `wide shot` in the KlingOmni column of src/lib/prompts/videoPromptGeneration.ts but to `wide establishing shot` in all four data/modelPrompt/video files.
conflicts.registryChoice: Both recorded under `modelTag`; unresolved, and pre-existing in the Chinese originals.

conflicts.what: The universal and Wan 2.6 modes call the prop asset type `prop`; the Seedance 2.0 mode calls it `tool` and adds `audio`. Both are schema enum values.
conflicts.registryChoice: Both listed as never-translate. Not resolvable from the i18n side.

conflicts.what: docs/i18n/glossary.json translates 已完成 as Completed / Đã hoàn thành. As a persisted state value it must never be translated.
conflicts.registryChoice: Recorded on the `dbEnum.completed` entry as `glossaryDivergence`. The glossary entry is correct for prose and must not be applied to a state value.

conflicts.what: docs/i18n/glossary.json gives the singular `sound effect`; the shipped en prompt files use `Sound effects` for the videoDesc field label.
conflicts.registryChoice: Registry follows the shipped plural, recorded as `glossaryDivergence` on `field.soundEffects`.

gaps.what: The emitting skill (data/skills/production_skills/storyboard_table_techniques.md) defines the cameraMove vocabulary as 推 / 拉 / 摇 / 移 / 俯拍 / 仰拍 plus 静止. The parsing prompts map 静止 / 推进 / 拉远 / 跟踪 / 摇镜 / 甩镜 / 升降 / 环绕. Only 静止 is common to both lists.
gaps.status: unresolved — a pipeline defect, not an i18n defect. The single-character values are not registered: they cross no boundary because the parser lists none of them.

gaps.what: 大远景 occurs 17× in the skills as a 景别 value but appears in no mapping table in the prompt layer.
gaps.status: not registered (single-layer). Recorded here so it is not mistaken for an oversight.

gaps.what: 固定 and 缓推 are emitted by the skills and used verbatim in the Seedance 2.0 worked example, but neither appears in any 运镜 mapping table.
gaps.status: registered (both layers contain them) and flagged in each entry's note.

gaps.what: The prompt spec writes `资产信息[id, type, name]` while the runtime emits `**资产信息**（角色、场景、道具、音频):`. The two have never matched, in zh either.
gaps.status: recorded on runtime.assetInfoLabel; the lockstep check only asserts the stem `资产信息` / `Asset info` / `Thông tin tài nguyên`.

signals: 全景深 is the photography term for deep focus (whole depth of field), usually next to an aperture such as f/8-f/11; the 全景 inside it is coincidental.
单张全景照片 / 全景摄影 mean a panoramic photograph of a whole space, not a shot size.
全景 in the 景别 column, or paired with 大全景 / 标准全景 as a framing variant name, IS the shot-size value.
homonymRisk.note: Counts prove nothing for this token: realpeople_modern_city/art_prompt/art_scene.md has 19 hits and NOT ONE is a shot size, while art_scene_derivative.md in the same style keeps 5 of 10 because 标准全景 there really is a framing variant. Decide per file.

signals: 分镜中景别 is a substring accident: the match straddles two words (…分镜中 + 景别…) and means nothing.
前景 / 中景 / 背景 as a series is about depth LAYERS in the frame, not shot size.
中景 in the 景别 column of a storyboard table, or in a 景别 mapping row, IS the shot-size value.
homonymRisk.note: 12 of the first pass's 40 allowances are for this token, split between the two false-positive shapes above.

homonymRisk.note: 9 occurrences across data/skills. 5 files keep it literal (translators wrote the gloss inline, e.g. "Medium and close shots (中近景)" in realpeople_urban_modern/prefix.md and realpeople_ancient_chinese/prefix.md, or the plain table-row value in realpeople_modern_city/README.md, director_storyboard.md, director_storyboard_table_style.md). 4 files translated the same 中近景提暖 phrase into pure prose without the gloss: 2D_90s_japanese_anime/prefix.md, 2D_mature_urban_romance/prefix.md, 3D_anime_render/prefix.md, 3D_clay_stopmotion/prefix.md. Both are acceptable — this token never crosses into data/modelPrompt/video or videoPromptGeneration.ts, so dropping the gloss in prose is a style choice, not a lost matched value; literalAllowance records the 4 that dropped it.
